items.problem: The namespace mapping table lumps the Windows.UI.Colors class move in with the Windows.UI.Xaml.* NAMESPACE moves, without warning that sibling Windows.UI types (the Color struct, Point/Size/Rect) do NOT move. A reader applying a blanket 'Windows.UI -> Microsoft.UI' mental model can either miss Colors or over-rewrite the struct.
items.evidence: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:112 '| `Windows.UI.Colors` | `Microsoft.UI.Colors` |' sits inside the 'All Windows.UI.Xaml.* namespaces move' table with no struct-stays caveat; the dev-agent kept Windows.UI.Colors and hit CS0234 (session-log.txt:2231).
items.proposed_improvement: Add a short caveat under the table: the moved-to-Microsoft.UI helper CLASSES are Colors and ColorHelper, whereas the Windows.UI.Color struct (and Point/Size/Rect) stay in Windows.UI — so never do a blanket Windows.UI->Microsoft.UI replace. Also add the ColorHelper row.
items.generalizes: The struct-stays / helpers-move split trips up every color-using migration; making the boundary explicit prevents both under- and over-rewriting across scenarios.
